fields.title: The writing skills state std-PROSE's rules a second time

sections.What we are doing instead:
[std-PROSE](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/0b33e205d64f9060cb2a2829d52c02981efd1834/examples/dog-fooding/standards/prose.md) is the record the estate cites for how prose is written here. The writing skills state the same rules for an agent, and cite no record:

* `technical-writing`, the floor every surface answers to
* `writing-a-record`, `writing-a-report`, `writing-in-the-tool` and `writing-the-docs`, one voice each

`manifest.yaml` sends `technical-writing`, `writing-a-record` and `writing-a-report` to every corpus built from the template. The other two stay in this repository.
sections.Why we need it: A corpus receiving the template may have no standards at all, so a skill linking to [std-PROSE](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/0b33e205d64f9060cb2a2829d52c02981efd1834/examples/dog-fooding/standards/prose.md) would send its agent to a page that is not there. A skill stating the rules itself works in any checkout. The alternative is a skill that works only here, and a corpus elsewhere that writes with no rules.
sections.What the risk is: The two copies drift. A rule changed in [std-PROSE](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/0b33e205d64f9060cb2a2829d52c02981efd1834/examples/dog-fooding/standards/prose.md) and left alone in a skill means an agent writes to the old rule, and a reviewer reading the standard sends the work back. Nothing checks that the copies agree. The cost falls on whoever reviews that agent's work.
sections.What compensates:
* [std-PROSE](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/0b33e205d64f9060cb2a2829d52c02981efd1834/examples/dog-fooding/standards/prose.md) names the writing skills in its Rationale, so whoever changes a rule there sees that a skill states it as
  well.
* [dev-one-maintainer](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/0b33e205d64f9060cb2a2829d52c02981efd1834/examples/dog-fooding/deviations/one-maintainer.md) is why the drift has cost little so far: the person changing the standard is the person who
  maintains the skills.
sections.How it closes: Every corpus that receives the skills also receives the standard, and each skill links its rules instead of stating them. That needs a way for the template to send a standard, and the template sends none today. Where the owner re-accepts this instead, the review weighs whether the skills and the standard have disagreed in practice.
sections.Scope: The writing skills under `.claude/skills/` and the copies `manifest.yaml` sends to each corpus. The skills a plugin bundles are outside it, because [std-PLUGIN](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/0b33e205d64f9060cb2a2829d52c02981efd1834/examples/dog-fooding/standards/plugin.md) has each of those quote the export and link the record for the rest.
